slides.0.title: Styles, WO labels and Cap Classique
slides.0.subtitle: The 85/85/100 rules and traditional-method sparkling
slides.1.title: The three numbers on a WO label
slides.1.highlights.0.title: Origin: 100%
slides.1.highlights.0.content: Grapes must be 100% from the stated area at every tier; blends across Wards go to District level, across Districts to Region level, and so on
slides.1.highlights.1.title: Cultivar: 85%
slides.1.highlights.1.content: A stated cultivar needs at least 85% of the wine; if no variety reaches 85%, list them in descending order totalling 100%
slides.1.highlights.2.title: Vintage: 85%
slides.1.highlights.2.content: A stated vintage needs at least 85% from that harvest; non-vintage wines (such as non-vintage Cap Classique and fortified wines) cannot carry a year
slides.2.title: The seal and label rules
slides.2.highlights.0.title: The WO seal (the "bus ticket")
slides.2.highlights.0.content: Issued after analysis and sensory evaluation with a unique number on the bottle neck; origin, variety, vintage and producer can be checked on the SAWIS site; since 1 August 2023 the issuing body is the Wine Certification Authority
slides.2.highlights.1.title: Estate Wine and Single Vineyard
slides.2.highlights.1.content: Estate Wine comes from bordering farms worked as a single unit and is made and bottled in the on-site cellar; a Single Vineyard must be one registered block of no more than 6 ha
slides.2.highlights.2.title: Reserve has no legal meaning
slides.2.highlights.2.content: Reserve, Grand Reserve and Limited Edition are unregulated and carry no standardised quality meaning
slides.2.content: Unlike in Europe, WO does not restrict varieties or methods; it guarantees the truth of origin, variety and vintage.
slides.3.title: Cap Classique
slides.3.highlights.0.title: Definition
slides.3.highlights.0.content: South Africa's bottle-fermented (traditional-method) sparkling wine; only wines meeting the rules may carry the term
slides.3.highlights.1.title: Minimum ageing
slides.3.highlights.1.content: At least nine months on the lees
slides.3.highlights.2.title: Growth
slides.3.highlights.2.content: In 2024 Cap Classique export value grew 19% and sparkling wine overall grew 34%
slides.3.content: Cap Classique's ageing minimum (nine months) differs from Champagne's; finer categories are still under discussion in the industry.
